candidates.angle: yatamanah, striving, shows effort is ongoing
anekajanmasamsiddhah, perfected through many births, shows ripeness
samshuddhalkilbishah, with impurities fully cleansed, shows purification

en.intro: Krishna answers the fear that effort can be lost. Listen to how the yogi moves from one birth to the next.
en.notice: The word yatamanah, striving, shows that the yogi is not resting on past skill. The effort is present, continuous, and active right now.
en.next: Krishna then places the yogi above all other paths of spiritual life.
en.meaning: But the yogi who keeps striving with effort, whose impurities have been cleared, and who has been perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अर्जुन के इस डर का उत्तर देते हैं कि क्या साधना व्यर्थ जा सकती है। सुनिए, एक जन्म से दूसरे जन्म तक योगी की यात्रा कैसे चलती है।
hi.meaning: परन्तु जो योगी प्रयत्नपूर्वक यत्न करता है और जिसके पाप नष्ट हो गये हैं तथा जो अनेक जन्मोंसे सिद्ध हुआ है, वह योगी फिर परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है।
hi.notice: योगी अपने पिछले ज्ञान पर विश्राम नहीं करता, उसका प्रयास निरंतर जारी रहता है।
hi.next: फिर कृष्ण योगियों को तपस्वियों और कर्मियों से भी महान बताते हैं।

issues: meaning_changed: "योगी अपने पुराने ज्ञान पर आराम नहीं कर रहा, बल्कि प्रयास निरंतर जारी है।" (The word 'बल्कि' (rather than) creates a contrast between resting on old knowledge and continuous effort. The source verse uses 'तु' (but) to connect the idea of striving with the other attributes of the yogi, not to contrast it with resting on old knowledge. This introduces a false opposition not present in the source.)

unsupported: "सुनिए, जन्म दर जन्म मार्ग कैसे बनता है।" (The phrase 'सुनिए, जन्म दर जन्म मार्ग कैसे बनता है' (Listen, how the path is built, birth by birth) is an unsupported factual claim. While the verse describes a yogi who is perfected through many births, it does not explicitly describe 'building' a path 'birth by birth'. The Sanskrit and standard Hindi translations focus on the yogi's state of being perfected over many lives, not the construction of a path.)
